title: החורים שנפערים בלילה על שפת ים המלח
summary: Dead Sea sinkholes: 6,000+ holes since the early 1980s (estimates vary) in a ~60 km strip; a ~10,000-year-old buried salt layer 20–70 m deep stayed safe because Dead Sea brine is saturated; as the sea falls >1 m/yr the fresh/saline groundwater boundary follows it, fresh groundwater reaches the salt edge, dissolves cavities, and the sand-and-mud roof collapses; Eli Raz (Ein Gedi geologist) fell into one, ~14 h, rescued by the team he founded; Mineral Beach; Nof & Baer 2013 InSAR mm-scale precursors; Jordan ~1,250 million m³/yr then <100 now, National Water Carrier 1964; maths: 600 km² × 1.1 m = 660 million m³/yr missing, shoreline retreat vs level drop.
reviewer_verdict: PASS (2 rounds) — nits left: time ~30–33 min, slightly over the 20–30 target (tag says כ־30 דקות); correct MCQ option is often the longest; Raz's 'documenting' wording leans on the Fox quote more than NBC; the review copy doesn't declare the sample capability, so Arto falls back there (template)
